title: Luke Skywalker Starred in a $4 Million PC Game in 1994
hook: In 1994 Wing Commander III put Mark Hamill, Malcolm McDowell and Biff from Back to the Future in a PC game with a reported $4 million budget, billed as the priciest game ever made. This week EA brought it back to Steam with its film scenes restored from tapes found in a vault. Did you ever fly a mission with Luke Skywalker?
script: Did you know Luke Skywalker himself starred in a PC game back in nineteen ninety four? Wing Commander began at Origin Systems in nineteen ninety, created by a young designer named Chris Roberts. It was a space combat game with a movie feel, and EA bought Origin in nineteen ninety two. Wing Commander Three, subtitled Heart of the Tiger, arrived in late nineteen ninety four and it was something new. It came on four CDs and told its story through filmed scenes with real Hollywood actors. Mark Hamill played the hero, Colonel Christopher Blair. Malcolm McDowell played Admiral Tolwyn, and John Rhys-Davies played Paladin. Tom Wilson, Biff from Back to the Future, played the cocky pilot called Maniac. The budget was reported at around four million dollars, and it was billed at the time as the most expensive game ever made. The sequel two years later cost a reported twelve million. Roberts later went to Hollywood and directed the Wing Commander movie in nineteen ninety nine. Then he created Star Citizen, which has now raised more than a billion dollars from players. And this week the old games came back. On November fifth, EA released twenty five classic PC games on Steam, including restored anniversary editions of Wing Commander. Their movie scenes were rebuilt from master tapes found in a storage vault. Did you ever fly a mission with Mark Hamill? Follow for more gaming history.
